findings.evidence: Real Helm accepts secretstore skipVerify=true; the retained Vault provider maps it to tls.Config.InsecureSkipVerify. Refuse this demonstrated certificate-verification bypass at the metadata boundary and cover safe false plus refused true values.

Carried from the earlier recorded rejection: equal endpointMetadataKey and credentialMetadataKey can produce invalid provider bindings, but this unusual environment-writer error fails at provider startup. Another guard is not warranted.

Real Helm accepts a repository containing team//app. Such malformed operator-supplied repositories fail loudly when consumed; extending repository parsing adds validation complexity for an unlikely input typo. Functional image readiness is excluded from this package qualification.

Real Helm accepts a configured path outside /etc/hexalith/environment; it would fail when the application opens the absent file. Environment writers own the supplied component-file contents, and a new generic path policy would add unsupported semantics without proving functional readiness.

The independently committed campaign environment topology validates only regular containers in supplied provider/reporter workloads. Init containers can bypass image, filesystem and resource checks; qualify this environment-owned campaign boundary separately from the application chart.

Real Helm accepts a 64-character endpoint DNS label. The shared DNS-subdomain helper also validates Kubernetes object references, whose contract differs; a separate authority-label guard adds complexity for an unlikely environment-writer error.

The concurrent v1 operator preparer and verifier use lexical is_relative_to checks without resolving dot segments or parent symlinks. A fresh apparent external path can resolve inside a repository and receive generated credential files. This independently authored operator custody path is outside Helm export qualification.

The concurrent v1 phase runner checks receipt absence before an ordinary write, with no execution lock in the caller. Two processes can both submit a supposedly single-attempt activation or seed phase; the separate operator runner needs serialization.

The concurrent v1 gateway path waits for Pod Running then polls HTTP, but request propagates connection-refused/timeouts and the attempted receipt prevents retry. A normal listener startup delay can permanently stop that operator phase; the read-only observation loop needs bounded transient retry.

The concurrent v1 main calls verify before every phase, and verify rejects an expired review before cleanup can inspect namespace ownership. Cleanup after the 24-hour authority window is therefore unavailable through that runner; its separate lifecycle needs an ownership-bound cleanup path.

The first verification reviewer demonstrated that all 22 chart tests pass with ACL namespaces hardcoded to reference. Add source/archive renders in a nondefault release namespace with complete ACL policy assertions. That reviewer disclosed reading spec claims; the independent replacement confirmed this gap.

The independent verification reviewer demonstrated that all 22 chart tests pass when the normal replica fallback is constant 1. Add direct source/archive assertions for accepted root replica values 2 and 3 across every normal Deployment.
Independently reproduced the same hardcoded ACL namespace regression gap as R6-VG-1. Group these two findings into the single nondefault namespace assertion patch.

Parent reproduced task-chart-template-drift in the synthetic operator render test. validate_profile requires canonical template byte equality, and this change left the tracked helper/application copies stale. Synchronize the two copies after the canonical helper fix and rerun that consumer suite.
